title: Indexes
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to pick one item from a list using its index number, starting from 0.
learn: Each item has an index position
Use -1 to get the last item
idea: Every item in a list has an index — its position. Python counts from 0, so the first item is list[0], the second is list[1], and so on. -1 means the last item. That is handy when you do not want to count the length yourself.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the first print from snacks[0] to snacks[2]. Press Run. The first line of output should say cookie.

practice.text: Make a list of three favorite movies. Print the first and the last using indexes.
practice.hint: The first movie is at index 0. For the last one, use movies[-1] or movies[2].
practice.starterTip: Try print(movies[0]) for the first and print(movies[-1]) for the last.
practice.starter:
movies = ["Up", "Coco", "Moana"]
# Print the first movie
print()
# Print the last movie (use -1)
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if two prints use indexes to show the first item and the last item (0 and -1 or 2).

practice.text: Print the middle item of this four-item list (index 1 or 2 — pick one and print it).
practice.hint: Index 0 is 10, index 1 is 20, index 2 is 30. Pick one of the middle numbers and use nums[that index] inside print.
practice.starterTip: Either print(nums[1]) to show 20 or print(nums[2]) to show 30.
practice.starter:
nums = [10, 20, 30, 40]
# Print one middle item
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if the program prints 20 or 30 using a list index.

quiz.question: A list has 4 items. What index does the last item have?
quiz.correct: With 4 items the indexes are 0, 1, 2, 3 — so the last is at index 3.
quiz.wrong: Indexes start at 0, so four items use indexes 0 through 3.

quiz.question: What does pets[-1] give you?
quiz.correct: Negative indexes count from the end, so -1 is the last item.
quiz.wrong: -1 means the last item in the list, not the first.

quiz.question: In ["a", "b", "c"], what is at index 1?
quiz.correct: Index 0 is a, index 1 is b, index 2 is c.
quiz.wrong: Remember: the first item is index 0, so index 1 is the second item.
